title: JavaScript Fundamentals
description: Types, scope, async, and the array methods you reach for daily.

questions.explanation: A longstanding bug kept for backwards compatibility: null's type tag is the object tag.

questions.prompt: Which array method returns a new array rather than mutating the original?
questions.explanation: map() builds a new array. push, sort, and splice all mutate in place.

questions.prompt: `const` prevents the contents of an object from being changed.
questions.explanation: const binds the variable, not the value — you can still mutate the object it points at.

questions.prompt: Which of these values are falsy in JavaScript? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: An empty array is an object, and all objects are truthy. 0, "", and NaN are falsy.

questions.prompt: What does an `async` function always return?
questions.explanation: An async function wraps its return value in a Promise, even if you return a plain value.

questions.prompt: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?
questions.explanation: `let` is block-scoped and reassignable; `var` is function-scoped; `const` can't be reassigned.

questions.prompt: What is the result of `"5" + 3` in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: With a string operand, + concatenates. `"5" - 3` would coerce to a number and give 2.
== coerces the string to a number, so 0 == "0". === doesn't coerce, and NaN is never equal to itself.

questions.prompt: Which array method gives you a single accumulated value from all elements?
questions.explanation: reduce() folds the array into one value using an accumulator.

questions.prompt: An arrow function has its own `this` binding.
questions.explanation: Arrow functions inherit `this` from the enclosing scope — that's the main reason to use one in a callback.

questions.prompt: Which of these create a new array or object rather than modifying the original? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Object.assign mutates its first argument. Spread, slice, and filter all produce something new.

questions.prompt: What does `await` do inside an async function?

options.text: Blocks the whole thread until the Promise settles
Pauses that function until the Promise settles, letting other code run
Converts a Promise into a callback
Retries the Promise until it resolves

questions.explanation: await suspends only the async function. The event loop keeps running everything else.

questions.prompt: What method turns a JSON string into a JavaScript object? (Give the full call, e.g. Thing.method)
questions.explanation: JSON.parse() reads a string into a value; JSON.stringify() goes the other way.

questions.prompt: What does `arr.find(fn)` return when nothing matches?
questions.explanation: find() returns undefined on no match. findIndex() is the one that returns -1.

questions.prompt: What is the `?.` operator called, and what does it do?

options.text: Optional chaining — short-circuits to undefined if the left side is null or undefined
Nullish coalescing — supplies a default value
Non-null assertion — tells the compiler a value exists

questions.explanation: `a?.b` gives undefined instead of throwing when `a` is null or undefined. `??` is nullish coalescing.
